attrs.title: Signs your Google Ads tracking needs fixing
attrs.lead: If any of these are true, Google is learning from the wrong numbers.

items.title: “Conversion tracking setup is incomplete”
items.text: Google Ads shows this warning when it hasn’t seen a conversion for a while or can’t find your tag. Usually the tag is missing, never fires, or fires on the wrong page, so smart bidding has nothing to learn from.

items.title: More conversions in Google than in your CRM
items.text: If Google Ads reports 200 leads and your CRM shows 110, something is counting twice: often the Google tag and an imported GA4 goal, or a thank-you page that reloads. Google then bids for leads that don’t exist.

items.title: Conversions dropped to zero after a site change
items.text: A redesign, a new theme, a new form plugin or a cookie banner can quietly break tags. Campaigns keep spending while bidding loses its signal, and costs climb within days.

items.title: Phone calls aren’t counted
items.text: For many businesses half the leads come by phone. Without call tracking, the campaigns that drive calls look as if they don’t work, and Google moves budget away from them.

items.title: Purchases with the wrong value, or counted twice
items.text: Missing values, the wrong currency or no transaction ID make your return on ad spend wrong, and value-based bidding starts chasing the wrong orders.

items.title: No idea which leads became customers
items.text: Every form fill counts the same, so Google finds more people who fill in forms, not more people who buy. Offline conversions from your CRM fix that.

attrs.noteTitle: Bad tracking costs more than bad ads
attrs.noteText: Smart bidding optimises towards whatever you tell it is a conversion. Fix the tracking, and every other change you make starts working better.

attrs.label: Set up, then tested on real actions
attrs.html:
Set up, then tested on real actions

Five steps over about two weeks. You see what we found and approve the plan before we build anything.

  1. We go through every conversion action in Google Ads, every tag and trigger in Tag Manager and every key event in GA4, and compare the numbers with your CRM or store for the same period.

    You get: A short audit of what’s broken and why.

    • Conversion actions, goals and counting settings reviewed
    • Tags, triggers and consent mode checked in Tag Manager
    • Google Ads numbers compared with your CRM or store
    • Duplicates, gaps and broken tags listed

  2. Together we decide what counts as a conversion, what each one is worth and which one Google should bid towards. Most setups skip this step, and it decides what smart bidding learns.

    You get: A one-page conversion map to sign off.

    • Primary and secondary conversions agreed
    • A value for each lead type or purchase
    • Counting set to one or every, per action
    • A tracking plan you approve before we build

  3. We build the tracking in Tag Manager or with the Google tag, add enhanced conversions and call tracking, and connect your CRM so sales flow back to Google Ads.

    You get: Tracking built in your own accounts.

    • Tags fired on the real action, not the page view
    • Enhanced conversions for web or for leads
    • Call tracking from ads and from your website
    • Click IDs captured with every lead for offline conversions

  4. We submit real test forms, make test calls and place test orders, then check each one arrives in Google Ads once, with the right value. Anything that fails is fixed and tested again.

    You get: Screenshots of every test conversion.

    • Every action tested on desktop and phone
    • Tag Assistant and Google Ads diagnostics checked
    • Values, currency and transaction IDs verified
    • Consent mode behaviour checked

  5. We walk you through what changed, hand over the test report, and check the numbers again two weeks later, once real conversions have come in.

    You get: The test report, yours to keep.

    • A 30-minute walkthrough with your team
    • The test report and conversion map
    • A follow-up check after two weeks
    • Notes on what to check after site changes

attrs.title: Why Google Ads tracking goes wrong
attrs.lead: A handful of problems cause most broken tracking. Here is what each one looks like inside the account, and how we fix it.

items.title: Conversions counted twice
items.problem: The Google tag and an imported GA4 goal both count the same form, so Google Ads reports twice the real number.
items.fix: One source of truth for each action, with the duplicate set to secondary so it no longer affects bidding.

items.title: Fired on page views, not actions
items.problem: The thank-you page can be reached from bookmarks, emails or a refresh, and every visit counts as a lead.
items.fix: Conversions fired on the actual form submit, with a check that the form really sent.

items.title: Broken by a redesign
items.problem: Tracking broke when the website was redesigned, and nobody noticed for weeks.
items.fix: Tags rebuilt in Tag Manager and tested on the new site, with an alert if conversions stop.

items.title: Every lead counts the same
items.problem: A student asking for a quote counts the same as a company ready to buy, so Google finds more of whoever fills in forms fastest.
items.fix: Offline conversions from your CRM, so Google learns which leads became customers.

items.title: Wrong purchase values
items.problem: Purchase values are missing, in the wrong currency or include tax and shipping, so return on ad spend is wrong.
items.fix: Values, currency and transaction IDs passed correctly from your store, and matched to your real revenue.

items.title: Calls not tracked
items.problem: Calls from ads and from the website aren’t counted, so call-driven campaigns look as if they don’t work.
items.fix: Call assets and website call tracking, with a minimum call length agreed with you.

attrs.title: What it’s like to work with us
Google Ads Conversion Tracking questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: How do I set up conversion tracking in Google Ads?
items.answer: Create a conversion action in Google Ads, add the Google tag or a Tag Manager tag that fires when the action happens (a form submit, call or purchase), then test it. Enhanced conversions and offline conversions improve accuracy further.

items.question: Why is my Google Ads conversion tracking not working?
items.answer: The most common causes are a tag that doesn’t fire on the real action, a broken trigger after a website change, consent settings blocking tags, or conversions counted twice through both the Google tag and GA4.

items.question: What does “conversion tracking setup is incomplete” mean?
items.answer: Google hasn’t received a conversion recently, or can’t find the tag on your site. It usually means the tag is missing, broken or never fires.

items.question: Do I need enhanced conversions?
items.answer: For most advertisers, yes. Enhanced conversions send hashed first-party data, such as email addresses, so Google can match more conversions despite cookie limits.

items.question: How do I import offline conversions from my CRM?
items.answer: Capture the Google click ID (GCLID) with each lead, then upload the lead’s outcome from your CRM to Google Ads. HubSpot and Salesforce can do this automatically.

items.question: Should I import GA4 conversions or use the Google Ads tag?
items.answer: Usually the Google Ads tag for primary conversions, because it’s faster and more accurate for bidding. GA4 conversions can be imported as secondary.
